title: Tracked .githooks dispatchers ship in every project's release archive
body:
# Tracked .githooks dispatchers ship in every project's release archive

## What happens

Since the guards adoption pass (23 Oct), `intent claude upgrade --apply` writes the commit gate's dispatchers into `.githooks/` and each project tracks them, so a clone receives them. Nothing marks them `export-ignore`, so `git archive` (a release tarball, GitHub's source archive, a Homebrew formula's url) carries `.githooks/` in every project that tracks them.

Measured 25 Oct on rhadamanth, read-only: these projects track `.githooks/` and `git check-attr export-ignore` answers `unspecified` for it: Anvil, Baize, Cdtempl, Conflab, Courses, Gtools, Intent, Lamplight, MicroGPTEx, Molt, Prodinfra, Prolix, Riffle, Trellis, Utilz.

Seen: Cdtempl's CI release-archive test failed (run 40223037015): "release archive top level changed ... actual: .githooks/ LICENSE.md ...". Cdtempl now export-ignores `.githooks/` by hand (b81c6fb). Elsewhere the dispatchers ship silently.

## Spec

- Canon owns this, once: wherever the upgrade writes the tracked dispatchers, it also ensures `.githooks/ export-ignore` in the project's `.gitattributes` (a marked block, as devbin does for its line endings), creating the file when absent. A project that wants the dispatchers in its archive opts out in its own lines.
- Doctor names a project that tracks `.githooks/` without the attribute.
- A test: after an upgrade in a fresh repo, `git archive HEAD | tar -t` lists nothing under `.githooks/`.
